lens: Small-size recognition and typography hierarchy; whole-frame still-image identity and coherence
evidenceInspected: Fresh full actual11 and owner-liked07; both hashes verified.
Native scene11 hero, workshop and tree-play crops; native07 hero/workshop comparisons.
Final11 companion 5x crop: plain Grok eye interiors and dark Muse eyes verified.
Owner Muse lineup, orange Clawd plush and original Grok reference.

score.scope: Whole-frame still-image identity, hierarchy, scale readability and coherent animated-film finish; no animation or audience-outcome score.
score.meaning: Strong, legible personal scene with preserved hero identity; repeated surface/contour breakup prevents a polished whole-image recommendation.

deductions.location: Hero forehead/cheeks, antenna edges and lower glasses rims; Clawd face; bench/workshop wood and tree
deductions.finding: 11 repeats angular seams, facets and irregular highlights across unrelated materials. Against07, the hero feels less softly finished and Clawd less distinctly plush. This weakens material separation and the controlled contours that carry the identity.

The seated companions are clear as a group, but Clawd’s watching intention relies mainly on placement because its face remains camera-facing. Dot has a clearer workshop-facing bias. This is a minor staging limitation, not a required anatomy change.

deductions.location: Path, grass and leaf detail surrounding the left/middle activities;420-width image
deductions.finding: Dense bright small marks compete with secondary gestures. At420, coding moth remains clear while the leaf game and exact workshop action collapse into small grouped shapes. Acceptable hierarchy, with limited narrative detail at this scale.

criteriaForNine: Restore controlled soft contours and differentiated materials across the whole frame: fine plush on cream/orange characters, coherent wood grain, smooth glasses and broad foliage planes; avoid the same angular crease treatment everywhere.
Preserve the current layout, V5 silhouette, three moth activities, four guests, flat Grok eyes and dark Muse eyes through that finish correction.
Check native material/contour integrity and1280/880/420 hierarchy together. Secondary actions may simplify, but the hero and scene groups must remain clear without enlarging guests.

strengths: The coding moth owns the right foreground at all three inspected scales; the path and tree arch connect the smaller left/middle activities without a competing foreground guest.
Cream head, unequal paddles, compact body, mitten hands and layered green wing shapes remain consistent with V5. Three activities still read as one character family.
Warm backlighting, reflected light, foreground foliage blur and a softer distant bridge establish a dimensional continuous park rather than a collage of isolated characters.
Muse/Grok share one leaf, Clawd and Dot have separate stools, and the moth/bench/MacBook relationship remains readable. The current eye corrections hold under magnification.

mustFix.location: Whole-frame finish, especially native hero and workshop crops
mustFix.action: Resolve the visible surface/contour breakup before presenting the entire image as polished. Use07’s softer material handling as a control while retaining11’s approved local eye/identity corrections; do not treat all surfaces with the same faceted texture.
mustFix.why: The requested finish concerns the entire animated-film world. Correct eyes and recognizable silhouettes alone do not resolve the inconsistent material language.

optional: Only if compatible with both visible square eyes, a subtle workshop-facing posture could clarify Clawd’s attention; do not repeat the rejected back-turn.
Quiet selected path/grass highlights around secondary actions if needed after material cleanup. Do not enlarge the supporting cast or add labels.
No further Muse hood/body redesign is justified by this inspection.
baselineComparison: 07 has smoother round glasses, gentler hero facial texture, softer orange Clawd fabric and more cohesive workshop surfaces.11 retains that composition and adds corrected Grok eyes and the restrained Muse treatment, but its pervasive sharp facets/creases are a visible finish regression. Neither baseline preference nor previous eye-only acceptance determines this whole-scene verdict.

pairDiscussion.scoreDifference: A weights material regression more heavily. Both retain their independently formed scores.
pairDiscussion.jointRecommendation: Both explicitly recommend revising whole-frame material and contour coherence before presenting the image as polished. Use07 as rendering-quality control, preserving11’s corrected eyes, V5 anatomy, current layout, three moth activities and four guests.
pairDiscussion.challengeAndResolution: B challenged a blanket removal of faceted detail. A explicitly agrees: retain intentional leaf planes and wood grain; remove the recurring polygon/crackle network crossing unlike materials. Do not use indiscriminate blur.

stagingClarification.initialPhrase: The seated companions are clear as a group, but their watching intention relies mainly on placement: Clawd remains camera-facing and the workshop action has no visible contact beat. This is a staging limitation, not a required anatomy change.
stagingClarification.resolution: B withdraws absence of an instantaneous hammer contact as a defect: the raised hammer is valid anticipation in a still. A agrees. The minor deduction concerns frontal Clawd attention only; its refinement remains optional.

pairDiscussion.skillWorkflowAgreement: Evidence from complete scenes, matched native material crops, local-scale reductions and magnified final eye checks serves distinct claims. Coherence principles do not mandate anatomy changes, erased texture or phone-readability assertions.
pairDiscussion.preservedLimits: No guest enlargement, additional cast, extra labels or further Muse redesign.420-width secondary-detail loss is not a demand to enlarge cameos.
pairDiscussion.approvalBoundary: Agreement on a required correction, not approval of unbuilt replacement artwork, the current full frame or a full18 outcome.
